Wir brauchen keine Filme wie „Terminator 2“ und dessen „Skynet“, um uns ein solches Szenario vorzustellen; wir schreiben das Jahr 2026, und es gibt bereits einen erschreckenden Präzedenzfall aus der Realität, der einen bewaffneten Konflikt mit dem atomar bewaffneten China hätte entfachen können.

Die als FAA NOTAM FDC 6/3825 bezeichnete Beschränkung trat am 18. September in Kraft und gilt bis zum 2. Oktober um 12:00 UTC. Sie umfasst einen Radius von 1,5 Seemeilen um das VORTAC-Gebiet von Waco und erstreckt sich von der Oberfläche bis zu einer Höhe von 10.000 Fuß über dem Boden.

Guest: Roger Köppel

Roger Köppel is Swiss, admires Germany — and is deeply concerned.

We are in “the most dangerous historical situation since the end of the Second World War.” And the owner of Weltwoche does not see the reason for this in what he considers supposedly aggressive behavior by Russia, but rather in what he describes as the West’s increasingly arrogant attitude.

“And, terribly, Germany is once again playing a very decisive role in all of this.”

A country that Germans once had every reason to be proud of. A “great country that has endured every imaginable abyss and every soaring high.”

And the former editor-in-chief of the German newspaper Die Welt is not saying this from afar. He knows Germany well, including from inside one of the country’s most important publishing houses. He has also accompanied Viktor Orbán to meet Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv and visited Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.

When you listen to the former member of the Swiss National Council speak, it is difficult not to be captivated. He talks about his admiration for Germany, a country that “practically survived its own downfall”; his frustration because it “distresses” him to see “what is happening there now”; and his warning that Germany risks escalating a conflict that, in his view, does not have to exist in this form.

I learned a great deal about democracy from a Swiss man: why Germany is held in such high regard abroad, why we may currently be in the process of jeopardizing that reputation, and how close we might actually be to a Third World War.

Are we really “so blinded by our own sense of goodness that we don’t even realize we are about to repeat the mistakes of the past,” as Roger Köppel puts it?
